parsed.english: There is a universal constant c > 0 such that for every finite nonlocal game G with nonempty answer sets and entangled value ω(G) < 1, and every n ≥ 1, the entangled value of the n-fold parallel repetition is at most exp(-c · (1-ω)^13 / ((1-ω) + log(|A||B|)) · n).
parsed.why_clearer: The hypothesis `0 < 1 - entangledValue G` becomes the more natural `entangledValue G < 1`, which matches the usual statement that the game is not perfectly winnable.
